en.title: ShoesNet — B2B Wholesale Footwear Marketplace App
en.description: Turned a wholesale footwear business running on a website and WhatsApp into a controlled ordering platform with real oversight of every vendor, product, and order.
en.problemHeadline: Wholesale business run like a retail storefront
en.problemBody: The business connected footwear factories to wholesale buyers, but the website was built like a retail storefront while the business ran on wholesale rules — buyers order by the carton, from one supplier at a time, at negotiated volume prices. The result was that orders lived in WhatsApp threads instead of the system, the owner had no way to stop a vendor from listing bad or misrepresented products, price changes could be disputed after an order was placed, and there was no reliable record of what was sold, to whom, or at what price. Growth meant more chaos, not more revenue.
en.diagnosisHeadline: The gap was control, not a shop window
en.diagnosisBody: The client didn't need a better shop window — he needed control. Three specific gaps were doing the damage: no gate on who joins the platform, no gate on what gets listed, and no locked record of the commercial terms at the moment a deal is struck. Everything else was a symptom.

en.title: Clean Basket — Mobile App Growth & Tracking Rebuild (Riyadh, KSA)
en.description: Rebuilt the measurement infrastructure and paid social strategy for a Saudi on-demand laundry app, scaling installs and in-app purchases to the point of operational over-capacity.
en.problemHeadline: Broken tracking made every ad dollar blind
en.problemBody: Tracking infrastructure was completely broken — no conversion data was flowing from the app to any ad platform. iOS was effectively invisible: SKAdNetwork was not configured, so Apple's attribution framework returned nothing, and in-app events like Add to Cart and Purchase were not mapped to any platform SDK, leaving all campaigns running with zero optimization signal. On top of that, campaigns across all three platforms had no coherent testing framework, no OS segmentation and no platform-specific creative strategy, with budget scattered against no clear performance benchmarks.
en.diagnosisHeadline: Measurement had to come before media spend
en.diagnosisBody: Measurement infrastructure was the foundation, not a technical detail. Without conversion signal reaching the ad platforms, no amount of budget or creative investment could produce reliable results — so the fix had to be sequenced foundation-first.

en.description: Rebuilt a Google Ads account for a Dubai aesthetic clinic, fixing broken tracking and restructuring campaigns by service to drive consistent daily appointment bookings.
en.problemHeadline: Broken tracking, no service-level ad structure
en.problemBody: Two problems defined the account. Conversion tracking was broken — bookings and form submissions were not recording correctly, so the campaign algorithm had no reliable signal to optimize against and budget was being spent without knowing what worked. Campaign architecture was also unstructured: all services were grouped together with no meaningful separation, making it impossible to optimize individual services independently, and there were no negative keyword lists at either service or brand level, leading to wasted spend on irrelevant queries.
en.diagnosisHeadline: Competitive category needed signal and segmentation
en.diagnosisBody: Medical aesthetics is one of the most competitive search categories in Dubai — high intent, high CPC and high customer lifetime value. Without accurate conversion signal and service-level segmentation, the account could not compete efficiently or match ad copy to search intent.
